headline: 5 districts on alert as heavy rain and landslide warnings issued
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department warns of torrential rain in Cox’s Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Chattogram due to a land depression.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has issued a warning for five southeastern districts, predicting heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours.
The affected areas include Cox’s Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Chattogram, where the torrential rain increases the risk of landslides in hilly regions.
The BMD stated that the weather system is caused by a land depression moving north-northwest over Myanmar and the adjoining northeastern Bay of Bengal.
The system is expected to gradually weaken as it continues its path, but it may bring gusty winds to the Chattogram and Cox’s Bazar ports.
Local warning signal No. 3 has been hoisted at these two ports to alert maritime activities.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to remain close to shore and operate with caution until further notice.
caption:
Heavy rain and landslide risks for 5 districts. The BMD warns of torrential rain in the southeast.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has issued a warning for five southeastern districts, predicting heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours.

The affected areas include Cox’s Bazar, Bandarban, Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Chattogram, where the torrential rain increases the risk of landslides in hilly regions.

The BMD stated that the weather system is caused by a land depression moving north-northwest over Myanmar and the adjoining northeastern Bay of Bengal.

The system is expected to gradually weaken as it continues its path, but it may bring gusty winds to the Chattogram and Cox’s Bazar ports.

Local warning signal No. 3 has been hoisted at these two ports to alert maritime activities.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to remain close to shore and operate with caution until further notice.

headline: 239 deaths as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: Nearly 2,000 more patients were hospitalised in a single day, bringing the total death toll this year to 239.
details: At least six more dengue patients died and 1,942 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am yesterday.
Of the recent deaths, three occurred in the Rajshahi division, while one each was reported in Dhaka South City Corporation, Dhaka North City Corporation, and the Dhaka division.
The total number of deaths this year has now risen to 239, with total cases reaching 77,672. Currently, 5,424 patients are receiving treatment in hospitals nationwide.
Experts attribute the rise to poor control of Aedes mosquito breeding, underreporting of infections, delayed hospitalisation, and repeated infections.
Public health expert Mushtuq Husain stated that sustainable control requires a long-term, coordinated, and people-centred public health programme rather than short-term drives.
Authorities have been urged to strengthen efforts to identify and destroy Aedes breeding grounds, particularly in densely populated urban areas, through regular monitoring.
Experts also stressed the need for better surveillance to identify infections early and for patients with warning signs to seek medical care promptly to prevent complications.
Greater public awareness is recommended to eliminate stagnant water around homes and workplaces, as repeated infections can increase the risk of severe dengue.
